title: Excerpt from Appellant's Brief, State v. Henderson
text:
No. 01-22-00789-CR

IN THE COURT OF APPEALS FOR THE FIRST DISTRICT OF TEXAS

HOUSTON, TEXAS

***

JAMES HENDERSON,
Appellant

v.

THE STATE OF TEXAS,
Appellee

***

On Appeal from the 230th Judicial District Court, Harris County, Texas
Trial Court Cause No. 1598763

***

APPELLANT'S BRIEF

TO THE HONORABLE COURT OF APPEALS:

COMES NOW, James Henderson, Appellant, by and through his undersigned counsel, and respectfully submits this brief in support of his appeal from the judgment of conviction entered on September 12, 2023.

STATEMENT OF FACTS

On the evening of February 14, 2023, Houston Police officers responded to a disturbance call at 1422 Elm Street, Houston, TX 77002. Upon arrival, they encountered Appellant James Henderson and the complainant, Maria Gonzalez. The State alleged that Appellant assaulted Ms. Gonzalez, causing bodily injury. Appellant maintained that he acted in self-defense after Ms. Gonzalez struck him first.

During the trial, the State called Officer David Thompson, who testified that he observed a laceration on Ms. Gonzalez's left arm. The defense called Appellant's neighbor, Arthur B., a minor whose identity was protected by the court and referred to by the initials A.B. A.B. testified that he saw Ms. Gonzalez throw a ceramic mug at Appellant before any physical contact occurred.

The trial court, presided over by the Honorable Judge Mitchell, admitted into evidence a text message from Appellant to Ms. Gonzalez, which the State argued demonstrated a motive. Appellant's counsel objected, arguing that the message was taken out of context.

After deliberating, the jury found Appellant guilty of assault causing bodily injury, a Class A misdemeanor. The court sentenced him to 180 days in county jail, suspended for 12 months of community supervision, and a fine of $2,000.

ARGUMENT

I. The Trial Court Erred in Excluding the Testimony of A.B. as Incompetent.

A.B. was a 13-year-old witness who observed the altercation from his front porch. The trial court, relying on Texas Rule of Evidence 601(a), found A.B. incompetent to testify due to his age, without conducting a proper voir dire. This was an abuse of discretion. See, e.g., Gonzales v. State, 4 S.W.3d 304, 310 (Tex. App.—Houston [1st Dist.] 1999, no pet.) (holding that a trial court must conduct a competency examination before excluding a child witness). The exclusion of A.B.'s testimony deprived Appellant of critical exculpatory evidence.

II. The Evidence Was Insufficient to Support the Conviction.

Appellant argues that the evidence was legally insufficient because the State failed to disprove self-defense beyond a reasonable doubt. Under Texas law, a person is justified in using force against another when and to the degree he reasonably believes the force is immediately necessary to protect himself from the other's use or attempted use of unlawful force. See Tex. Penal Code § 9.31(a). The record shows that Ms. Gonzalez admitted on cross-examination that she was angry and had consumed alcohol. A.B.'s excluded testimony would have corroborated Appellant's claim that Ms. Gonzalez initiated the physical confrontation. Without this evidence, the jury's verdict is not supported by the record. See Jackson v. Virginia, 443 U.S. 307, 319 (1979).

CONCLUSION

For the foregoing reasons, Appellant respectfully requests that this Court reverse the judgment of the trial court and remand for a new trial, or in the alternative, render a judgment of acquittal.

Respectfully submitted,

/s/ Patricia L. Nguyen
Patricia L. Nguyen
State Bar No. 24056789
Nguyen & Associates, PLLC
1422 Elm Street, Suite 300
Houston, TX 77002
(713) 555-0123
